F001.text: Hola, me llamo Marina. Hoy es sábado y estoy muy contenta.

M011.text: Hello, my name is Marina. Today is Saturday and I am very happy.

F002.text: Esta noche Laura, mi compañera de la clase de cocina, viene a cenar a mi casa.

M012.text: Tonight Laura, my classmate from the cooking class, is coming to my place for dinner.

F003.text: Por la tarde limpio el salón y pongo la mesa.

M013.text: In the afternoon I clean the living room and set the table.

F004.text: Pongo un mantel blanco, dos platos y unas flores amarillas.

M014.text: I put on a white tablecloth, two plates and some yellow flowers.

F005.text: Quiero una cena perfecta para mi amiga.

M015.text: I want a perfect dinner for my friend.

F006.text: A las seis empiezo a cocinar.

F007.text: El gazpacho ya está hecho y está en la nevera.

M017.text: The gazpacho is already made and it is in the fridge.

F008.text: Ahora preparo una tortilla de patatas.

M018.text: Now I am making a Spanish potato omelette.

F009.text: Pelo las patatas y corto una cebolla.

M019.text: I peel the potatoes and cut an onion.

F010.text: Después bato seis huevos en un bol.

M020.text: Then I beat six eggs in a bowl.

F011.text: Frío las patatas despacio en aceite de oliva.

M021.text: I fry the potatoes slowly in olive oil.

F012.text: Luego llega el momento más difícil: dar la vuelta a la tortilla.

M022.text: Then comes the hardest moment: flipping the omelette.

F013.text: Uso un plato grande y… ¡ay! La tortilla se rompe en dos.

M023.text: I use a big plate and… oh no! The omelette breaks in two.

F014.text: ¡Qué apuro! Laura llega en media hora.

M024.text: How embarrassing! Laura arrives in half an hour.

M025.text: I think: "And now what do I do?"

F016.text: A las ocho y media suena el timbre.

M026.text: At half past eight the doorbell rings.

F017.text: Abro la puerta y allí está Laura, con una gran sonrisa.

M027.text: I open the door and there is Laura, with a big smile.

F018.text: Trae una tarta de queso hecha por ella.

M028.text: She brings a cheesecake she made herself.

F019.text: «¡Hola, Marina! Esto es para el postre», dice.

M029.text: "Hi, Marina! This is for dessert," she says.

F020.text: Yo digo: «¡Qué bonita! Muchas gracias. Pasa, pasa».

M030.text: I say: "How lovely! Thank you very much. Come in, come in."

F021.text: En la cocina le enseño la tortilla rota.

M031.text: In the kitchen I show her the broken omelette.

F022.text: «Mira, se ha roto. ¡Qué vergüenza!», le digo.

M032.text: "Look, it broke. How embarrassing!" I tell her.

F023.text: Laura se ríe y me pone la mano en el hombro.

M033.text: Laura laughs and puts her hand on my shoulder.

F024.text: «No te preocupes. ¡Las tortillas rotas también están buenas!»

M034.text: "Don't worry. Broken omelettes taste good too!"

F026.text: Laura se pone un delantal y me ayuda.

M036.text: Laura puts on an apron and helps me.

F027.text: Ella prepara una ensalada con lechuga y tomate.

M037.text: She makes a salad with lettuce and tomato.

F028.text: Yo sirvo el gazpacho en dos cuencos.

M038.text: I serve the gazpacho in two bowls.

F029.text: Hablamos de la clase de cocina y de la profesora.

M039.text: We talk about the cooking class and the teacher.

F030.text: Cocinar con una amiga es muy divertido.

M040.text: Cooking with a friend is a lot of fun.

F031.text: A las nueve nos sentamos a la mesa, al lado de la ventana.

M041.text: At nine we sit down at the table, next to the window.

F032.text: Hay gazpacho, tortilla, ensalada y pan.

M042.text: There is gazpacho, omelette, salad and bread.

M043.text: We raise our glasses and make a toast.

F036.text: Primero probamos el gazpacho. Está muy fresco.

M046.text: First we taste the gazpacho. It is very fresh.

M048.text: She smiles and gives a thumbs-up.

M049.text: "It's delicious! Broken, but delicious," she says.

F041.text: Después de la cena, preparo dos cafés.

M051.text: After dinner, I make two coffees.

F042.text: Laura corta la tarta de queso.

F043.text: Es suave y no muy dulce.

M053.text: It is soft and not very sweet.

M054.text: I ask her: "Will you give me the recipe?"

M055.text: She answers: "Of course! It's very easy."

F046.text: Salimos al balcón con los cafés.

M056.text: We go out onto the balcony with our coffees.

F047.text: Es de noche y Madrid tiene muchas luces.

M057.text: It is night and Madrid has lots of lights.

F048.text: Hace un poco de fresco, pero se está muy bien.

M058.text: It is a little chilly, but it is very nice out here.

F049.text: Hablamos de nuestros planes para el verano.

M059.text: We talk about our plans for the summer.

F050.text: Laura quiere ir a la playa y yo quiero visitar a mis padres en Valencia.

M060.text: Laura wants to go to the beach and I want to visit my parents in Valencia.

F051.text: A las once volvemos a la cocina.

M061.text: At eleven we go back to the kitchen.

F052.text: Yo lavo los platos y Laura los seca.

M062.text: I wash the dishes and Laura dries them.

F053.text: Hay mucha espuma y nos reímos otra vez.

M063.text: There are lots of bubbles and we laugh again.

F055.text: Yo digo: «¡Vale! El próximo sábado, en tu casa».

M065.text: I say: "OK! Next Saturday, at your place."

M066.text: She answers: "And I'll make a paella."

F057.text: A medianoche Laura se va a casa.

F058.text: Le doy un poco de tortilla en un táper.

M068.text: I give her some omelette in a plastic container.

F059.text: Nos damos un abrazo en la puerta.

M069.text: We give each other a hug at the door.

F060.text: Pienso: la tortilla no es perfecta, pero la noche sí.

M070.text: I think: the omelette isn't perfect, but the evening is.

M071.text: What a lovely evening with my friend!

M001.text: Welcome! Marina is back. Tonight her cooking classmate Laura comes to her flat for dinner, and Marina makes a Spanish omelette. What could go wrong? Listen first with Spanish subtitles.

M002.text: Now listen again. Each Spanish line is followed by its English translation.

M003.text: Now listen one last time, without story subtitles.

M004.text: Here are three questions. Answer in Spanish. You will have five seconds after each one.

M005.text: Now, sixteen useful words from the story. Spanish first, then English.

M006.text: Now, three expressions you will hear in Spain.

M008.text: Tell me in the comments: what do you like to cook for your friends?

M009.text: Subscribe, so you do not miss Marina's next story.

M010.text: Hasta la próxima, and see you next time!

S01e.text: "¡Qué apuro!" means "how embarrassing!" You say it when you feel awkward in front of someone.

S01x.text: ¡Qué apuro! Laura llega en media hora.

S02e.text: "No te preocupes" means "don't worry". You say it to make someone feel better.

S02x.text: «No te preocupes. ¡Las tortillas rotas también están buenas!»

S03e.text: "¡Buen provecho!" means "enjoy your meal!" In Spain people say it before eating, and the answer is "¡Igualmente!"
